title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Discover free social activities and public spaces at Boston College, from historic reading rooms to scenic reservoir walks and campus traditions.

cards.title: Browse the McMullen Galleries
cards.subtitle: Brighton Campus
cards.notes: Visit this world-class art museum on the Brighton Campus. Admission is always free for students and the general public to view rotating exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A university art museum offering free public admission to its permanent collection and rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the McMullen Museum is always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit – McMullen Museum of Art - Boston College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 10am-5pm, Saturday-Sunday 12pm-5pm during the academic year.

cards.title: Study in Gargan Hall
cards.subtitle: Bapst Library
cards.notes: Experience the 'Harry Potter' vibes of this silent study hall. It features stained glass and vaulted ceilings, providing a majestic free workspace.
cards.short_summary: A historic, neo-Gothic silent study hall located on the top floor of Bapst Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Bapst Library offers 400 quiet study spaces... Gargan Hall (top floor of Bapst) has great architecture.
cards.access_notes: Public access typically allowed during daytime hours; BC ID required after 10pm.

cards.title: Walk the Reservoir Loop
cards.subtitle: Chestnut Hill Reservation
cards.notes: Jog or walk the 1.5-mile paved perimeter trail. It offers iconic views of the Gasson Hall tower and the Boston skyline at no cost.
cards.short_summary: A popular 1.5-mile public walking and running loop adjacent to the Boston College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Enjoy a walk, jog, or bike ride on the 1.5 mile paved trail around the Chestnut Hill Reservoir.
cards.access_notes: Public park open from dawn to dusk daily.

cards.title: Join the Convocation Flight
cards.subtitle: Middle Campus
cards.notes: Participate in the 'First Flight' tradition. Freshmen carry lanterns down these stairs to Conte Forum to mark the start of their journey.
cards.short_summary: A university tradition where freshmen process down the Higgins stairs during Convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Freshman Eagles begin their BC journey with the traditional 'first flight'—a lantern-led procession down the Higgins stairs.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor stairs accessible 24/7; tradition occurs annually in the fall.

cards.title: Lounge at Stokes Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Stokes Hall
cards.notes: Relax on the tiered grass seating in front of Stokes Hall. It is a prime spot for outdoor socializing and sunbathing between classes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor tiered lawn and gathering space located in the center of the academic quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Stokes Amphitheater. The lawn in front of Stokes... a perfect location for studying.
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space accessible to the public 24/7.

cards.title: Attend a Public Lecture
cards.subtitle: Devlin Hall
cards.notes: Catch a free guest lecture or film screening in this large auditorium. Many academic events here are open to the entire BC community.
cards.short_summary: A major campus lecture hall that hosts free public academic and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Devlin Hall, 110. New Lecture. Free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Event times vary; check the university calendar for free public listings.

cards.title: See the Skyline from O'Neill
cards.subtitle: O'Neill Library
cards.notes: Head to the top floor of the main library for some of the best free views of the Boston skyline and the campus quads.
cards.short_summary: The highest floor of the main campus library, known for its panoramic views and quiet study area.
cards.evidence_claim: 5th floor of O'Neill has great views of the city.
cards.source_title: Any college libraries open to the public - Reddit
cards.access_notes: Open 7am-11pm for the public; BC ID required for late-night access.

cards.title: Relax on St. Mary's Lawn
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Quad
cards.notes: Find a quiet bench on this manicured lawn. It is a peaceful 'oasis' perfect for reading while listening to the Gasson Hall bells.
cards.short_summary: A serene green space located between St. Mary's Hall and O'Neill Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: The lawn outside of St. Mary's Hall is perhaps my favorite lawn on campus... an oasis of serenity.
cards.source_title: The Best of Boston College's Outdoor Spaces - BC Heights

cards.title: Take a Free Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation
cards.notes: Full-time undergrads can join group fitness classes like yoga or HIIT for free. Just sign the waiver in the Agora Portal first.
cards.short_summary: The university's main fitness facility offering free group classes to undergraduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation offers group fitness classes to all members free of charge... All full-time BC undergraduate students are eligible.
cards.access_notes: Requires BC ID and signed membership agreement for student access.

cards.title: Explore the Arts Festival
cards.subtitle: O'Neill Plaza
cards.notes: Enjoy three days of free music, dance, and theater performances every April. Most events are held in tents on the O'Neill Plaza.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring festival showcasing student and faculty creative works through free public performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Boston College Arts Festival... features music, dance, theater, visual arts, and more. It's a great opportunity to enjoy some incredible performances.
cards.source_title: End the Semester With These Fun (and Free) Events - BC Heights
cards.access_notes: Annual event in late April; most performances are free and open to the public.
